claims.text: A 2–5 at.% Al and 1–3 at.% Cr addition to Mg-Nb-Ti powder will produce a transient Mg-Al-Cr eutectic liquid below 850 °C.
The transient liquid will enable liquid-phase sintering within 850–900 °C without bulk melting.
Liquid-phase sintering in this window will cause rapid densification.
Processing in the proposed window will suppress Mg volatility.
The proposed processing will drive formation of a metastable, homogeneous, single-phase BCC solid solution.
Rapid cooling will suppress nucleation of brittle Laves/C14 intermetallics.
Brittle C14 Laves phases increase cracking and deteriorate alloy properties.
The high specific surface area of the starting powders makes them prone to oxidation.
Mg volatility becomes significant above 800 °C.
Applying 50–100 MPa will suppress Mg vaporization.
The transient liquid lowers the activation energy for diffusion and accelerates homogenization of Nb and Ti.
The transient liquid wets the powder and eliminates porosity.
Al and Cr promote formation of a dense, adherent protective oxidation film at high temperature.
A protective Cr2O3/Al2O3 mixed scale will form rapidly during the low-oxygen sintering dwell.
Cr can be prevented from segregating into Laves phases by kinetic trapping in the BCC solid solution or by incorporation into protective oxides.
The optimized alloy will exceed 99% relative density.
Conventional powder-metallurgy sintering can leave residual porosity that degrades properties.
Failure to form a dense protective oxide scale causes exponential oxidation weight gain.
Below 850 °C, insufficient liquid formation and diffusion will cause porosity above 5%.
Above 925 °C or beyond a 30-minute dwell, Mg evaporation will cause elemental loss, microstructural collapse, and loss of barrier properties.

contradictions.description: The process requires an Ar atmosphere with less than 10 ppm O2 to minimize oxidation, yet the mechanism requires rapid growth of a dense Cr2O3/Al2O3 scale during the same short sintering dwell. The oxygen source and means of obtaining a continuous scale under these conditions are not specified.
The hypothesis describes a protective Cr/Mg-oxide barrier, whereas the mechanism specifies a Cr2O3/Al2O3 mixed barrier and does not explain the role or presence of Mg oxide.

The predicted density is greater than 99%, but the density-based falsification threshold is only failure to exceed 98%. A result between 98% and 99% would fail the prediction without satisfying the stated density falsification rule.
